structured_output.reasoning: The incident shows two concrete scope violations: (1) the agent performed a broader rewrite when the frustrated message says "a rewrite was not requested," and (2) the follow-up complaint confirms the agent worked outside the requested workspace ("You did not use the /work/fake-lantern workspace requested"). The proposed remedy text explicitly calls out both failure modes: "do not expand it into a broader rewrite or rebuild" and "do not work in a different location than requested" when a request specifies "a single file, a single change, a specific workspace/location, or specific required output fields." This is a direct, word-for-word match to the two things the user complained about in this incident, not just a loosely related principle. The remedy is a standing global instruction (claude-md), so it would be loaded in future sessions and plausibly steer the agent to confine work to the named location and avoid unrequested rewrites. There's no indication of a gap left uncovered by this specific incident's evidence — both surfaced complaints (rewrite scope, wrong workspace) are named verbatim in the remedy text.
